questions.q: Define Class in Java.
questions.model: A class is a template (blueprint) used to create objects and define the data type. It is a building block of Java's object-oriented systems.

questions.q: What do JDK, JRE and JVM stand for?
questions.model: JVM = Java Virtual Machine; JRE = Java Runtime Environment; JDK = Java Development Kit.

questions.q: What is the difference between a syntax error and a logical error?
questions.model: Syntax errors break the grammar of the language so the compiler cannot compile the file. Logic errors compile and run but the program does not do what the programmer expects.

questions.q: Can you override a private or static method in Java? Explain.
questions.model: No. A private method is not accessible in the subclass, so it cannot be overridden (a same-named method there is a new method). A static method belongs to the class; a same-signature static method in a subclass HIDES the parent's method (method hiding) rather than overriding it.

questions.q: What are the various access specifiers for Java classes? Give 4 examples.
questions.model: public: accessible from anywhere. protected: same class, same package and subclasses. default (no modifier): same package only. private: same class only.

questions.q: Write a for loop that prints all the multiples of 3 from 3 to 36 (3 and 36 included).
What is the difference between break and continue statements?
questions.model: break exits the loop immediately. continue skips the rest of the current iteration and moves on to the next iteration.
